state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you explain why you chose Triangle as the net of the shape shown in the image? What characteristics of the shape are you considering when determining the correct net?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought it was a Triangle because the shape kind of looks like it has three sides, and I guess I just focused on the pointy part. But now I'm confused because I see the circle and the sector, and I'm not sure how they fit together. Can you help me understand what the net really shows?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you identify the different parts of the shape shown in the image? How does each part contribute to the overall structure of the 3D shape?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so I see the circle and the sector now, and I think the circle is like the base of the shape. The sector looks like it could wrap around to make the sides. But I'm still not sure how they all fit together to make a 3D shape. Is it like a cone or something?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses questioning to maintain cognitive demand and the student progresses from seeing a triangle to correctly identifying a cone's net, though the scaffolding could be more targeted to the specific visualization difficulty with how nets fold into 3D shapes.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking without ever directly stating the answer, asking the student to identify parts, explain reasoning, and consider how components relate to the overall structure—a textbook example of Socratic method.
